hypothesis: The current pitch group is hidden at inference, but its selection distribution is predictable from legal pre-pitch context and frozen pitcher history. Four strong exact-C outcome experts, marginalized by a CatBoost pitch-group model, can recover stable control difficulty that a single global outcome tree averages away.

relationship_to_prior_work.e22_mixture: same probabilistic factorization but the old experiment used an SGD pitch selector and the weak S4 Linear/HGB parent rather than exact-C CatBoost outcome experts
relationship_to_prior_work.trackman_lupi: the recent LUPI test appended probabilities and imputed physics as ordinary global-tree features; it did not fit group-conditional exact-C experts or explicitly marginalize them
relationship_to_prior_work.pitchtype_failure_prior: the prior used smoothed failure-rate tables, not strong group-conditional outcome models

deployment_contract.historical_expert_label: pitch_type_group from official 2019-2024 TrackMan rows matched to historical main rows
deployment_contract.inference_mixture_weights: CatBoost probabilities fitted only on historical matched rows and scored from the current row's legal pre-pitch fields

diagnostic_oracle_contract.purpose: measure whether current pitch group contains enough signal before attributing failure to the deployable selector

selection.locked_rule: maximize the minimum full-score gain across both development years and all anchors among trials with positive R point gain and positive R pitcher-cluster CI lower bound in every cell
